findings.text: 面向需要动态插件、依赖变化与确定性清理的 Rust 应用开发者，提供运行时基础设施；它不是现有 DSH 可直接加载的插件。
typed prepare在准入前形成Input，spawn建立精确realm依赖与驻留事务，稳定后交付FiberHandle；服务publication和事件登记归属当前generation，dispose完成清理与精确unlink，见 [Q02](#research-q02)。
完整统计仅覆盖本工程工具支持的Markdown和JS/TS，本库主要Rust源码不在统计口径，不能据空代码分组推断规模为零。研究抽读Rust core准入、服务、事件和清理及示例，未执行编译、测试或应用；未全面检查update/era/timer/loader或独立验证TS等价。
Cargo workspace：facade cordis-rs0.11.1，core/timer/loader0.6.1；MIT，Rust1.88与2024 Edition声明。它是应用依赖，不是原生DSH bundle；未核实实时crates可取得性或发布制品与固定提交对应关系。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rust >=1.88及2024 Edition | 集成必需，Cargo声明 | 类型化框架编译 | 本轮未编译，不能把声明当兼容通过 |
| Tokio及core基础依赖 | 运行必需 | 异步执行、同步和错误处理 | 阻塞poll仍会拖延生命周期与cleanup |
| cordis-rs0.11.1与core0.6.1 | facade使用需配套 | 保留cordis导入名并重导出core | 跨0.5/0.6类型不能混用 |
| timer、loader | 对应功能可选 | 时间操作或声明式加载 | core不自带这些叶子能力；本轮未核查全部实现 |
| 应用持有句柄和业务补偿策略 | 正确关闭必需 | dispose与外部副作用恢复 | Drop不自动关Fiber，无全Runtime shutdown |

开发诊断工具链固定为1.98.1，与最低支持版本含义不同；依赖和版本边界见 [Q04](#research-q04)。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次集成 | 编译、依赖及运行资源，金额未知 | 学习typed契约、改写组件、资源登记和句柄管理 | 无集成人时实测 |
| 持续运行 | 运行时内存、任务与依赖变化开销未知 | 版本配套和诊断处理 | 不能以Rust类型约束推断更快或更省资源 |
| 失败恢复 | 重试与外部补偿资源未知 | 区分Pending、apply失败、cleanup失败和进度停滞 | 框架清理不回滚数据库或远端业务写入 |
| 升级与退出 | 重编译及应用资源，金额未知 | 非穷尽枚举/版本迁移，关闭roster及退回原路径 | 当前为预冻结破坏性版本线，不能只换依赖号 |
先在隔离Rust应用里选一个确需动态依赖的组件，显式保存FiberHandle并安排关闭；检查缺依赖Pending、服务realm、apply失败和清理诊断。不要将realm当沙箱，也不要直接用于DSH安装。遇到错误回退、重复清理或关闭卡住就停止扩展，保留原有应用路径及最小复现；先确认配套版本和维护支持范围，见 [Q04](#research-q04)。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
|---|---|---|
| 准入与交付 | prepare分离、驻留提交和Active/Pending交付实现 | 所有并发交错和真实应用可靠性 |
| 服务放置 | 指定realm的精确查询及publication撤回 | 应用是否正确分配所有服务，非租户安全认证 |
| 清理所有权 | 一次性领取、LIFO和终态屏障 | 失败cleanup是否关闭外部资源、永不完成清理的时限 |
| 开发与运行收益 | 无同条件应用结果 | 节时、性能、维护成本及ROI |
可借鉴的是准入提交点与CreationGuard、服务publication的精确身份撤回及generation一次性清理journal。这些机制将所有权放在显式位置，而不是依赖隐含Drop。代价是创建future进度条件、异步清理与应用关闭策略必须一起理解；观察记录只作诊断，不能当业务回放和授权系统，见 [Q03](#research-q03)、[Q05](#research-q05)。
相对手工异步装配，它把配置准备、生命周期准入、精确服务放置及资源清理绑定到有类型的运行时契约，并明确交付与终态屏障。概念继承Cordis体系，已有增量是Rust环境中的语义组织，不是新的Agent能力或已验证性能优势，见 [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02)。
显式清理不等于自动关闭应用。丢弃Handle不会dispose，创建future仍存活但不poll会停住，真正drop才交接未交付创建的清理；已登记cleanup失败也不证明外部资源关闭。realm与Scope更不是恶意插件或租户安全边界，见 [Q03](#research-q03)。
应用层可尝试关联创建、交付及终态unlink轨迹，并以实际资源探针核验退出。用不poll、不同阶段drop、cleanup失败和依赖撤回样本比较错误终态解释与定位耗时；任何把Pending当Active或错误证明资源已关闭的轨迹都削弱假设。该方向未验证，见 [Q05](#research-q05)。

business.rationale: workflow25%=9：[Q04](#research-q04) teardown:9-26把应用关闭和插件资源登记责任写成明确分工，相对零散回调有局部开发流程改善；未改变实际业务任务组织或交接结果，不取50%。delivery25%=8：[Q02](#research-q02) spawn交付Active/Pending句柄与dispose终态屏障提供有限可验收组件契约；没有新的终端业务交付单元，未达50%。reach25%=5：[Q01](#research-q01) facade lib:1-12给Rust开发者提供Cordis风格契约，是有限语言接入增量；仍需Rust异步与迁移知识，不支持普通DSH安装人群，不取50%。economics0%：[Q04](#research-q04) 仍由应用维护句柄、版本及补偿，相对手工Tokio未识别独立资源调度、定价或服务成本结构变化，不取25%；不是把未测人时记零。

recommendation.reason: 正在构建动态插件式 Rust 守护进程的开发者可以在隔离应用中试用一个带服务依赖与清理的组件。相对手写 Tokio 状态和回调，这个框架提供准备、准入、精确服务放置和显式终态契约，可靠性与维护收益仍未实测。出现依赖缺失仍执行、错误服务回退、重复清理或关闭无法完成时，开发者应停止扩展并退回原有应用路径与最小复现。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) README:7-14描述长期插件与服务变化，Plugin及spawn源码对应明确的反复启停和清理摩擦，超过50%用途描述；没有独立应用需求和持续采用材料，不取100%。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) spawn:252-376、service:774-868与[Q03](#research-q03) effect:130-177给出超出单入口的类型和所有权增量，超过25%；相对手工方案无运行对照且有进度条件，不取75%的结果改善档。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 入口prepare/spawn、服务与事件到[Q03](#research-q03) dispose闭环有固定源码，并明确不poll与Drop反例，超过25%片段；没有本次编译或并发执行，上限50%，不取75%。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04) Cargo:17-39、README:45-61及teardown:9-26明确版本、迁移和关闭责任，隔离应用及原路径为退路，超过25%负担与恢复不明；预冻结破坏性版本、支持文档不一致及手动补偿，不满足75%低且可预测负担。

publication.summaries.text: 为长期运行的 Rust 应用提供插件生命周期、服务依赖、类型化事件及资源清理框架。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| Rust插件准入与句柄 | typed准备后创建并管理长期组件 | 需应用编译集成；不是DSH插件入口，Pending不代表可用 |
| 精确服务realm | 按服务名选择实例放置与查找 | 无缺失回退，不是权限白名单或恶意代码隔离 |
| 类型化事件 | 显式Routing下派发组件通信 | Scope与服务realm独立，Unscoped不做Scope筛选 |
| generation资源清理 | 一次性领取已登记cleanup并显式dispose | 仅已登记义务，应用持有Handle且处理外部副作用 |

publication.advice.text: 先在隔离Rust应用里选一个确需动态依赖的组件，显式保存FiberHandle并安排关闭；检查缺依赖Pending、服务realm、apply失败和清理诊断。不要将realm当沙箱，也不要直接用于DSH安装。遇到错误回退、重复清理或关闭卡住就停止扩展，保留原有应用路径及最小复现；先确认配套版本和维护支持范围，见 [Q04](#research-q04)。

        "question": "generation 清理和隔离究竟保证什么，何时仍需应用兜底？",
        "status": "answered",
        "answer": "generation提供的是已登记资源的生命周期所有权，不是对任意外部副作用的事务回滚。清理journal按提交顺序编号，用remove领取某个occurrence的唯一义务；drain按逆序领取并逐项await，错误或panic被规范化并报告后继续。Fiber dispose先取得终态所有权，交给CallerDriven完成清理、Disposed发布和精确驻留unlink；并发调用等待相同终态屏障。这是比“Drop就当结束”更明确的完成契约。\n\n应用仍必须保存需要结束的FiberHandle并显式dispose；仓库没有全Runtime shutdown，丢Context或Handle不构成生命周期teardown。spawn出的Fiber没有隐含父子销毁关系，可以活得比发起者久。另一个关键区别是创建future：提交后仍存活但不再被poll会停在创建中，依赖它的删除也会等；真正drop该future才把未交付Fiber的清理交给框架。不能笼统宣称所有postcommit操作都自动前进。dispose自己的已提交owner则有独立前进的实现。\n\napply或cleanup若阻塞执行线程、外部服务永不响应，依然会影响进度；Plugin契约要求每次poll不阻塞，用户应把同步阻塞移出异步工作线程。attempt-all只表示前一项返回失败后继续，不能保证永不完成的清理有时间上限。清理失败被消费并形成诊断，不等于外部资源已成功关闭。\n\nrealm和Scope约束同一进程内的服务放置及事件可达性，不是恶意插件隔离、租户认证或OS沙箱。try_service并不要求先声明inject，拿到更广Context的可信代码仍能使用相应服务；Unscoped事件也绕过Scope筛选。若应用需要多租户授权、资源配额或远端命令撤销，必须在应用和执行边界另行实现。",

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "# Cordis\n\n**English** | [简体中文](https://github.com/dshbox/cordis-rs/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md)\n\n[![CI](https://github.com/dshbox/cordis-rs/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dshbox/cordis-rs/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n\nCordis is a typed runtime for long-lived, plugin-oriented Rust applications.\nIt gives application components one model for lifecycle, service dependencies,\ntyped events, resource cleanup, and explicit isolation boundaries.\n\nCordis is useful when your program is more than a collection of short-lived\nfunction calls: plugins can appear and disappear, services can become available\nor unavailable, configuration can change, and runtime resources must still be\ncleaned up deterministically.\n\n## Install\n\nFor applications, keep the historical package and import identity:\n\n```toml\n[dependencies]\ncordis-rs = \"0.11\"\ntokio = { version = \"1\", features = [\"rt-multi-thread\", \"macros\"] }\n```\n\n```rust\nuse cordis::Context;\n```\n\n`cordis-rs` is now a thin application-facing facade over the v3 runtime contract.\nFramework and plugin authors may depend on that contract directly:\n\n```toml\n[dependencies]\ncordis-core = \"0.6\"\n```\n\nOptional capabilities stay explicit semantic dependencies:\n\n```toml\ncordis-timer = \"0.6\"\ncordis-loader = \"0.6\"\n```\n\nCordis v3 requires Rust **1.88** or newer and uses Rust 2024 Edition.\n\nWhen upgrading from semantic `0.5` / facade `0.10`, update core, timer and loader\nrequirements together to `0.6` and the facade to `0.11`. The facade re-exports\ncore types; mixing `0.5` and `0.6` core types causes type mismatches. `0.6` is a\nbreaking pre-freeze line: public vocabularies expected to grow are now\n`#[non_exhaustive]` (add wildcard arms and `..` patterns), Loader source rows are\nextensible and built with `PluginEntry::new` and `EntryGroup::new`, and two\ndocumented promises are narrowed (creation progress after its commit, and the\nmeaning of lifecycle admission order;\n[ADR 0029](docs/adr/0029-lifecycle-commits-complete-and-critical-sections-are-closed.md)).\nThe compatible-evolution rules, enum openness and auto-trait and operation-future\n`Send` promises are recorded in\n[ADR 0042](docs/adr/0042-public-evolution-declares-openness-and-auto-traits.md).\nFor step-by-step edits and earlier\nupgrades, see [MIGRATION.md](MIGRATION.md), the\n[core release notes](crates/cordis-core/CHANGELOG.md) and the\n[facade release notes](crates/cordis/CHANGELOG.md).\n\n## Migrating from 0.6.x\n\n`cordis-rs 0.11.x` is the current application-facing v3 release line. The v3\narchitecture first shipped on the `0.7.x` line. The `0.6.x` implementation remains\non the `legacy/0.6` maintenance branch for\ncritical bug and security fixes. The v3 transition is intentionally breaking;\nsee [`MIGRATION.md`](https://github.com/dshbox/cordis-rs/blob/main/MIGRATION.md) and [`docs/v3-migration.md`](https://github.com/dshbox/cordis-rs/blob/main/docs/v3-migration.md).\n\n## The mental model\n\nFive types carry most of the public model:\n\n- **`Context`** — a cheap immutable view into one Cordis Runtime.\n- **`Plugin`** — reusable behavior with typed source configuration and runtime input.\n- **`FiberHandle`** — the lifecycle handle for one admitted non-root Fiber.\n- **`Service`** — a typed, named capability published into an exact service realm.\n- **`Event`** — a typed runtime communication contract with explicit routing.\n\nA Plugin enters the Runtime through a deliberate boundary:\n\n```text\nConfig\n  │\n  │ Plugin::prepare()\n  ▼\nInput\n  │\n  │ PreparedPlugin::from_input(...)\n  ▼\nPreparedPlugin\n  │\n  │ Context::spawn(...)\n  ▼\nFiberHandle / Fiber\n```\n\n`prepare()` runs before lifecycle admission. `spawn()` is the first operation\nallowed to create Runtime lifecycle state.\n\n## Quick start\n\nThe smallest complete flow is: define an Event, define a Plugin, prepare and\nspawn it, dispatch the Event, then explicitly dispose the returned FiberHandle.\n\n```rust\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\n\nuse cordis::event::{ListenerRegistrationError, observer_sync};\nuse cordis::{BoxError, Context, Event, Plugin, PreparedPlugin, Routing};\n\nstruct Ping;\n\nimpl Event for Ping {\n    const NAME: &'static str = \"ping\";\n    type Args = String;\n    type Output = ();\n}\n\nstruct Echo;\nstruct EchoInput;\n\nimpl Plugin for Echo {\n    type Config = ();\n    type Input = EchoInput;\n    type PrepareError = Infallible;\n    type ApplyError = ListenerRegistrationError;\n\n    fn prepare(&self, (): ()) -> Result<Self::Input, Self::PrepareError> {\n        Ok(EchoInput)\n    }\n\n    async fn apply(\n        &self,\n        ctx: Context,\n        _input: &Self::Input,\n    ) -> Result<(), Self::ApplyError> {\n        let _listener = ctx.on::<Ping, _>(observer_sync(|_, name| {\n            println!(\"hello, {name}\");\n            Ok::<_, Infallible>(())\n        }))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), BoxError> {\n    let ctx = Context::new();\n\n    let plugin = Echo;\n    let input = plugin.prepare(())?;\n    let prepared = PreparedPlugin::from_input(plugin, input);\n    let fiber_handle = ctx.spawn(prepared).await?;\n\n    ctx.emit::<Ping>(Routing::Unscoped, \"world\".into()).await?;\n\n    fiber_handle.dispose().await?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\nRun the repository's complete version with:\n\n```bash\ncargo run -p hello_plugin\n```\n\n## Lifecycle and convergence\n\nA successful `Context::spawn()` returns a `FiberHandle` only after the new Fiber has\nsettled for the current service snapshot. The stable result is normally:\n\n- **Active** — all required Services are available and `apply()` succeeded.\n- **Pending** — a required Service is currently unavailable; `apply()` has not run.\n\nRequirements are declared with `InjectSpec`. They are lifecycle prerequisites,\nnot constructor injection. When an exact required Service publication appears or\ndisappears, Cordis converges affected Fibers toward their new stable state.\n\nA `FiberHandle` exposes the main lifecycle operations:\n\n- `ready()` waits for the current stable state.\n- `restart()` reapplies the current committed input on the same Fiber.\n- `update(PreparedChange)` attempts a precommit-controlled typed input replacement; a committed update keeps the same Fiber.\n- `era_swap(PreparedChange)` performs identity-breaking replacement; a successful successor has a fresh Fiber identity.\n- `dispose()` ends the Fiber and runs its cleanup.\n\nDropping a `FiberHandle` does **not** dispose the Fiber. Lifecycle ownership is explicit.\n\nResources registered through a Plugin's apply `Context` are owned by that apply\ngeneration. Listener registrations, Service publications, tasks, effects, and\ntimer operations can therefore be cleaned up with the generation instead of\nbeing manually threaded through application code.\n\n\n## Application teardown\n\nCordis deliberately has no Runtime-wide shutdown API. Applications retain the\ndelivered `FiberHandle`s they intend to end and call `dispose().await` during\nnormal shutdown. The demonstrated example Harness records handles in spawn order\nand disposes them in reverse spawn order, attempt-all; that ordering is\napplication policy, not a hidden Fiber parent/child relation.\n\nDropping a `FiberHandle` or `Context` is ordinary Rust Drop, not lifecycle teardown,\nand root-owned registrations do not disappear merely because Context clones are\ndropped. See [Application teardown](docs/application-teardown.md) for the\ncomplete demonstrated pattern, including repeated teardown, generation cleanup,\nand Loader handoff ownership.\n\n## Services: exact placement, not fallback lookup\n\nA Service is identified by its semantic Service name and resolved from one exact\nslot:\n\n```text\n(Service, ServiceRealm)\n```\n\nBy default a Context uses the Runtime's default realm. Isolation changes the\nrealm selected for specific Service names.\n\nTo give one Service a fresh private slot:\n\n```rust\nlet tenant_a = root.with_isolated_service(Database::NAME);\n```\n\nTo isolate several Services, chain the operation:\n\n```rust\nlet tenant_a = root\n    .with_isolated_service(Database::NAME)\n    .with_isolated_service(Cache::NAME)\n    .with_isolated_service(Ledger::NAME);\n```\n\nEach call changes only that Service's placement. Other Service mappings are\ninherited.\n\nFor explicit sharing and joining, allocate opaque realms and map Service names to\nthem:\n\n```rust\nlet shared_metrics = root.new_service_realm();\nlet tenant_a_db = root.new_service_realm();\nlet tenant_b_db = root.new_service_realm();\n\nlet tenant_a = root.with_service_realms([\n    (Database::NAME, tenant_a_db),\n    (Metrics::NAME, shared_metrics.clone()),\n])?;\n\nlet tenant_b = root.with_service_realms([\n    (Database::NAME, tenant_b_db),\n    (Metrics::NAME, shared_metrics),\n])?;\n```\n\nNow the tenants resolve different Databases but the same Metrics slot.\n\nA `ServiceRealm` is only an opaque Runtime-local placement identity. It has no\nhierarchy, parent lookup, textual rendezvous, or fallback rule. If a Context maps\n`Database` to a private realm and that realm has no visible Database publication,\nlookup is unavailable; Cordis does not fall back to the default realm.\n\n## Events: typed communication with explicit Scope routing\n\nAn `Event` declares a Runtime-local semantic name together with typed `Args` and\n`Output`. Listener adapters make the listener role explicit:\n\n- **Observer** — notification side effect.\n- **Responder** — may answer a query.\n- **Mapper** — transforms a waterfall payload.\n- **Around** — onion-style middleware with a consuming `Next`.\n\nDispatch always chooses routing explicitly:\n\n```rust\nctx.emit::<Ping>(Routing::Unscoped, payload).await?;\n\nctx.emit::<Ping>(Routing::Scoped(request_scope), payload).await?;\n```\n\n`Routing::Scoped(scope)` reaches scoped registrations on the target Scope itself\nand its ancestors, plus global registrations. {\n        self.inner.lock().current\n    }\n\n    fn publish(&self, next: FiberState) -> Option<FiberState> {\n        let old = {\n            let mut inner = self.inner.lock();\n            let old `deadline::tests` proves that on an isolated scheduler.\n    }\n}\n\n/// Successor-specific cause of a committed era replacement that could not hand off a fresh Fiber.\n#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]\n#[non_exhaustive]\npub enum EraSwapFailure {\n    /// The fresh successor's initial apply failed after allocation.\n    #[error(\"successor apply failed: {0}\")]\n    SuccessorApply(PluginFailure),\n    /// Framework invalidation prevented delivery of the fresh successor.\n    #[error(\"the fresh successor was lost before handoff\")]\n    SuccessorLost,\n}\n\n/// Failure of one identity-breaking fresh-era replacement attempt.\n#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]\n#[non_exhaustive]\npub enum EraSwapError {\n    /// Candidate belongs to another Plugin contract.\n    #[error(\"prepared change targets a different plugin contract\")]\n    PluginContractMismatch,\n    /// The source Fiber was already closing or terminal before the source claim.\n    #[error(\"fiber is closed\")]\n    Closed,\n    /// Lifecycle recursion was refused before the source claim.\n    #[error(\"{0}\")]\n    Recursion(LifecycleRecursion),\n    /// The source claim committed, but no successor can be handed off.\n    #[error(\"era replacement incomplete: {0}\")]\n    Incomplete(EraSwapFailure),\n}\n\n/// Successful outcome of one typed same-Fiber update attempt.\n///\n/// Precommit control may veto without reaching lifecycle commit.       "content": "# Application teardown\n\nThis page is application-author guidance. The normative lifecycle and ownership\ncontracts remain in [`docs/v3-public-interface.md`](v3-public-interface.md) and\nADRs [0028](adr/0028-fiber-generations-own-cleanup-runtime-owns-residency.md)\nand [0029](adr/0029-lifecycle-commits-complete-and-critical-sections-are-closed.md).\n\n## The short version\n\nCordis deliberately has no Runtime-wide shutdown operation. An application owns\nits teardown policy:\n\n1. retain every delivered `FiberHandle` whose Fiber the application intends to\n   end;\n2. on normal shutdown, call `dispose().await` for those handles;\n3. when order matters, compose that order in the application; the demonstrated\n   Harness/Roster policy is reverse spawn order; and\n4. attempt every planned disposal instead of stopping after the first refusal.\n\n`FiberHandle::dispose().await` is the deterministic lifecycle end for one\nnon-root Fiber. Return means its terminal barrier has completed: the current\ngeneration is closed and drained, `Disposed` has been published, and the exact\nRegistry residency occurrence has been unlinked.\n\nThere is no equivalent `Runtime::shutdown()`, and dropping a `Context`,\n`LoadOutcome`, or `FiberHandle` is not a substitute for lifecycle teardown.\n\n## A demonstrated application policy\n\nThe repository's consumer-of-record Harness records delivered handles in spawn\norder and tears them down in reverse order:\n\n```rust\nuse cordis::{FiberHandle, FiberState};\n\nasync fn teardown(fibers: &[FiberHandle]) {\n    for fiber in fibers.iter().rev() {\n        if fiber.state() == FiberState::Disposed {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fiber.dispose().await {\n            eprintln!(\"teardown refused for {}: {error}\", fiber.name());\n            // Attempt the remaining Fibers.\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\nThat order is **consumer composition policy**, not hidden parenthood in core.\nSpawning a Fiber records provenance but creates no parent/child lifecycle\nownership. A spawned Fiber can outlive the Fiber whose Context initiated the\nspawn.       "content": "//! hello_plugin — the on-ramp seat: the smallest correct Cordis program.\n//!\n//! A [`Plugin`] prepares typed source configuration before lifecycle admission.\n//! [`PreparedPlugin`] then seals that input value to the Plugin contract, and\n//! [`Context::spawn`] performs the complete lifecycle transaction before handing\n//! the consumer a live quiescent [`cordis_core::FiberHandle`]. The consumer keeps that\n//! FiberHandle in its Harness roster and deterministically disposes it at teardown.\n//!\n//! Run with `cargo run -p hello_plugin`.\n\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\n\nuse cordis_core::event::{ListenerRegistrationError, observer_sync};\nuse cordis_core::{BoxError, Context, Event, Plugin, PreparedPlugin, Routing};\nuse examples_common::{Roster, section};\n\n// 1. Declare an event: one Runtime-local name with one typed contract.\nstruct Ping;\n\nimpl Event for Ping {\n    const NAME: &'static str = \"ping\";\n    type Args = String;\n    type Output = ();\n}\n\n// 2. Define a Plugin with explicit unit source configuration. Even unit\n//    configuration is prepared into a typed input before lifecycle admission; no builder,\n//    default config, erased config, or raw lifecycle input is involved.\nstruct Echo;\n\nstruct EchoInput;\n\nimpl Plugin for Echo {\n    type Config = ();\n    type Input = EchoInput;\n    type PrepareError = Infallible;\n    type ApplyError = ListenerRegistrationError;\n\n    fn prepare(&self, (): ()) -> Result<EchoInput, Infallible> {\n        Ok(EchoInput)\n    }\n\n    async fn apply(&self, ctx: Context, _input: &EchoInput) -> Result<(), Self::ApplyError> {\n        // 3. Register typed Plugin behavior. The returned exact-occurrence\n        // capability may be dropped inertly because the Fiber generation owns\n        // cleanup; deterministic FiberHandle disposal removes the registration.\n        let _listener = ctx.on::<Ping, _>(observer_sync(|_, name| {\n            println!(\"  hello, {name}\");\n            Ok::<_, Infallible>(())\n        }))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), BoxError> {\n    let ctx = Context::new();\n    let mut roster = Roster::new();\n\n    // 4. Prepare explicitly, seal the exact Plugin/input association, then\n    //    perform complete spawn. A successful handoff is already live and\n    //    quiescent; the Harness records the delivered FiberHandle for teardown.\n    section(\"boot: one echo plugin\");\n    let plugin = Echo;\n    let input = plugin.prepare(())?;\n    let sealed = PreparedPlugin::from_input(plugin, input);\n    roster.push(ctx.spawn(sealed).await?);\n    roster.report().await;\n\n    // 5. Dispatch is typed and routing is explicit. The Plugin behavior is\n    //    observable as \"hello, world\".\n    section(\"run: emit Ping\");\n    ctx.emit::<Ping>(Routing::Unscoped, \"world\".into()).await?;\n\n    // 6. Consumer-owned teardown deterministically disposes the delivered FiberHandle.\n    section(\"teardown: dispose the FiberHandle\");\n    roster.teardown().await;\n\n    // The listener was generation-owned: after disposal there is no callback.\n    ctx.emit::<Ping>(Routing::Unscoped, \"nobody listens anymore\".into())\n        .await?;\n    println!(\"  (the second Ping printed nothing — the listener died with the FiberHandle)\");\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"
